sources.title: Mathematical discoveries from program search with large language models
sources.authors_note: Bernardino Romera-Paredes, Mohammadamin Barekatain, Alexander Novikov, et al.; complete author list retained at source
evidence_supported: FunSearch pairs a pretrained language model with a systematic evaluator in an evolutionary program-search loop.
For the cap-set problem, the paper reports new constructions that improve on previously known results in finite-dimensional and asymptotic settings.
For online bin packing, the paper reports heuristics that improve on widely used baselines.
The evaluator scores generated programs and retains correct high-scoring programs, separating candidate generation from systematic evaluation.
The article received, accepted, publication, version-of-record, and issue dates are publication-process dates and do not by themselves establish exact internal candidate-generation dates.

sources.title: FunSearch: Making new discoveries in mathematical sciences using Large Language Models
evidence_supported: DeepMind publicly announced FunSearch on the Nature publication date.
The announcement describes FunSearch as a language-model-plus-evaluator loop that iteratively evolves executable programs.
It separately describes cap-set discoveries and online bin-packing heuristics, supporting later tranche-02 splitting rather than treating the aggregate seed event as one undifferentiated result.

The announcement states that generated cap-set programs produced previously unknown constructions and that the bin-packing program used fewer bins than established heuristics in the described evaluations.

candidate_generation_date.rationale: The current primary record establishes publication-process chronology but does not establish when individual cap-set constructions or bin-packing heuristics were first generated internally. The seed year remains a coarse proxy and is not silently recoded.

evidenced_verification_processes.process: cap-set result comparison against best-known constructions
online bin-packing heuristic comparison against established baselines

verification_date.rationale: Automated evaluator checks, result-specific comparisons, and journal peer review are distinct verification processes. Current evidence does not justify collapsing them to one verification date.

public_disclosure_date.rationale: Nature publication and the DeepMind first-party announcement occurred on 2023-12-14.

acceptance_date.publication_process_note: Nature manuscript acceptance occurred 2023-11-30 but is not silently recoded as disciplinary acceptance.

technology_dependency.rationale: The reported results were generated by the FunSearch language-model-plus-evaluator search system, while problem specification, evaluator design, interpretation and publication retained human roles.

candidate_children.comparison_baseline: best-known cap-set constructions at the time of the reported experiments
established online bin-packing heuristics reported in the primary article

aggregate_event_separation.split_rule: Do not assign one aggregate discovery or verification date to both child result families without result-specific primary evidence.

notes: The seed candidate-generation year is retained as a coarse proxy rather than silently sharpened.
The seed publication date is supported by the primary article.

remaining_questions: Locate primary evidence that bounds result-specific candidate-generation dates before the manuscript received date.
Split cap-set and bin-packing outcomes into result-level tranche-02 records with separate comparisons and verification surfaces.
Collect independent reproduction, downstream adoption, critique, supersession, or performance-regression evidence for each result family.
Identify whether individual cap-set dimensions or bin-packing program variants warrant separate child records.
